title: Why do these two arms never make a triangle?
description: A base of five centimetres is drawn with ninety degrees at both ends, and then with one hundred degrees and ninety five degrees. In both cases the arms do not meet. Keeko's doubt is that longer arms will meet.
teaching_notes: One idea: when both base angles are ninety degrees or more, the arms stand side by side or lean apart, so they cannot meet. Watch for students who think that drawing the arms longer makes them meet.

source: Say why no triangle can be built from the angles 90°, 5 cm, 90° and from 100°, 5 cm, 95°.
video_script.why: The child can draw a triangle from two angles and the side between them and now finds that some pairs of angles give no triangle.
video_script.substitution: The book's own sets: a base of five centimetres with ninety degrees at both ends, and with one hundred degrees and ninety five degrees.
video_script.anchor: a base of five centimetres with ninety degrees at both ends, and with one hundred degrees and ninety five degrees
video_script.wrong_answer: the arms will meet if we draw them long enough
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko draws both arms very long and expects them to meet far away, but arms that stand side by side keep the same gap and arms that lean outwards get further apart.
video_script.payoff_line: Two angles of ninety degrees or more always give arms that never meet

final_answer.value: no triangle, angles of 90° or more
final_answer.spoken: no triangle can be built, because two angles of ninety degrees or more give arms that never meet

maths_rules: 90°, 5 cm, 90°: both arms stand straight up from the base, side by side, and the gap stays 5 cm, so they do not meet
100°, 5 cm, 95°: both arms lean outwards from the base, so the gap grows, and they do not meet
when both angles are 90° or more the arms do not meet, and so no triangle can be built
video_script.design: One base is drawn twice, once for each set of angles. The gap between the two arms is shown with a double arrow at three heights, so the child sees it stay the same or grow.
